note: One composer per idea, one idea per beat. Pick by the transformation you want, not by habit. A beat is 4–13 s; a chapter is 3–5 beats. Never repeat a composer in consecutive beats, and never use two dense UI beats back to back — vary the viewpoint (wide shot, user view, close-up, inside-view).

coldOpen.draws: A finished shot holds the frame, breaks into picture / sound / voice / captions, and folds back into one line.
coldOpen.use: The hook. Use it first when the point is that a finished video is made of parts you control.

layerFlow.draws: The four layers leave the frame and become four lanes that converge on one timeline.
layerFlow.use: The bridge from the concept to the tool. Hand it off to a UI beat.

reveal.draws: The product name resolves out of the timeline geometry, camera pushes, one line of value under it.
reveal.use: Name the product after the hook, once, with no feature list.

editorBuild.draws: The editor window builds itself: bin, inspector and timeline fill, clips drop in, gaps close.
editorBuild.use: Show the real editing surface for the first time.

editActions.draws: A clip is trimmed, split and snapped while the timecode and snap badge track the action.
editActions.use: Prove the editor does exact-frame work, not a mock-up.

cutRipple.draws: One cut ripples the whole track: clips shift, the gap closes, the playhead stays honest.
cutRipple.use: Show a single destructive-looking edit that is actually reversible.

layersAlign.draws: Picture, sound, voice and captions slide onto the same frame; a mismatch snaps back into sync.
layersAlign.use: The sync idea, stated visually before it is named.

previewExport.draws: The viewer plays, the export sheet opens with 1080p / Matroska / 30p, a progress bar fills.
previewExport.use: The end of the edit: a real deliverable, not a render farm promise.

assistantScope.draws: The open project is the scope: a request in words points at the real timeline behind the chat.
assistantScope.use: Establish that the assistant reads the project, not a blank chat.

chatAsk.draws: A selected clip, a short request, and a harness chip light up beside the composer.
chatAsk.use: The moment a request is made. Keep the request one sentence.

assistantRole.draws: The assistant proposes an edit and a caption; the human approves; the work is repeatable.
assistantRole.use: State the division of labour: assistant proposes, human decides.

acpBridge.draws: A beam crosses the ACP boundary: project → CLI / MCP → harness, with provider keys staying on the near side.
acpBridge.use: The integration story. Only show a harness the build supports.

harnessRail.draws: A rail of installed harnesses; OR does not install them and does not hold their keys.
harnessRail.use: Be precise about what the app does and does not ship.

chatResult.draws: The result card returns: what was added, where it landed, one line of confirmation.
chatResult.use: Close the assistant chapter with a visible change in the project.

motionCode.draws: A code pane types a scene; each line lifts off and becomes a shape on the stage.
motionCode.use: The first code-to-video beat. Keep the code short enough to read.

motionBuild.draws: The shapes assemble a shot: horizon, light, subject; fills sweep in; the camera settles.
motionBuild.use: Show the scene being built, not a finished still.

motionMorph.draws: The built shot morphs frame by frame; geometry changes form while the camera keeps moving.
motionMorph.use: The deterministic payoff: every frame is a function of time.

motionTimeline.draws: The rendered scene lands on the timeline as an ordinary clip beside real footage.
motionTimeline.use: Prove the scene is editable material, not a special case.

ttsScript.draws: script.json opens; the chosen local voice card sits beside it; engine and sample rate are named.
ttsScript.use: The narration chapter opener. Name the real engine and voice.

ttsWave.draws: The waveform fills as the line is spoken; the voice clip lands on its track at the measured time.
ttsWave.use: Show the voice becoming a clip, with exact timing.

whisperListen.draws: Whisper listens locally: language badge, mic rings, a duration that matches the WAV.

whisperCues.draws: Proposed cues appear beside the waveform; a human reviews and applies them to the caption track.
whisperCues.use: The subtitle path from audio, with the human check kept in frame.

workflowLoop.draws: One loop on one machine: script → voice → transcript → captions → timeline.
workflowLoop.use: Close the production chapter by showing the closed loop.

freeLicense.draws: The MIT licence line, then a per-run cost meter that stays at zero for local work.
freeLicense.use: State free precisely, including what still costs.

mitDoc.draws: The licence document, then a split: what MIT covers and what it does not.
mitDoc.use: Correct the assumption that MIT makes every dependency free.

localCost.draws: A local bill: electricity, disk, time — no per-token meter.
localCost.use: The cost beat. Numbers on screen, no hand-waving.

ownership.draws: The projects folder sits on the user's disk; the app has no account gate.
ownership.use: The ownership feeling after the licence facts.

reality.draws: The current release card: version, date, platform, signing status, what is missing.
reality.use: The honesty beat. Never skip it in a product film.

releaseCard.draws: A release stamp: 0.1.0, macOS, Apple Silicon, arm64, .dmg.
releaseCard.use: Pin the facts the film claims to a version.

platformGap.draws: A phone outline with 'cần máy thật' and a missing-assistant badge.
platformGap.use: Show a real limitation without apologising for it.

mobileQuestion.draws: The mobile gap becomes a harness question: one agent system vs dozens of integrations.
mobileQuestion.use: Explain the design constraint behind the gap.

providerTrap.draws: One harness chip against a wall of twelve provider chips that would each need feeding.
providerTrap.use: The 'why ACP' argument, as a comparison.

notarize.draws: The .dmg card with ad-hoc signed / not notarized stamps and the right-click-to-open step.
notarize.use: The install reality. Keep the instruction exact.

checks.draws: CI checks run on a real runner: same commit, same command, honest green/grey states.
checks.use: Evidence beat. Show what was not run as clearly as what was.

community.draws: The main branch: one person starts, many people make it better.
community.use: Open the community chapter with the human claim.

contribPath.draws: A contribution path: issue → diff + notes → review → main, with the MIT and Apple Silicon gates.
contribPath.use: Make contributing concrete, not a slogan.

commitment.draws: A pull request conversation: a real question, a fix, a merge.
commitment.use: Show the social contract of review.

close.draws: Mark and wordmark, one-line value, the honest licence line, one call to action.
close.use: The last beat. Brand, what it is, what it costs, what to do next.
